SNACS adaptation notes (v2.6)

Annotate adpositions with [scene role, lexical function]. The role captures the relation in context; the function captures the preposition's construal. Identical labels are common; use a distinct function only when guidelines/examples motivate it.

Possessive determiners can have different scene roles even when all function Gestalt. In “my back” where back is a body part, Whole;Gestalt. In “my fusions” (an event/state associated with the experiencer), Theme;Gestalt. In “my experience” meaning what the speaker experienced, Experiencer;Gestalt. Do not collapse all “my” into Possessor: Possessor is for an alienable possessor relation; body part/whole is Whole.

Temporal “after” locating an event relative to another time/event: Time;Time.

“of” in a quantity construction like “an amount of time” links the measure noun to what is measured: QuantityItem;Gestalt.

“for” introducing the intended audience/customer or purpose of a recommendation (e.g. recommend them for any custom lighting): Purpose;Purpose.

Useful distinctions: Characteristic is for properties of entities; Manner describes events. Event/state change endpoints use Source or Goal, not Characteristic. PartPortion is incomplete relative to a whole; Stuff fully comprises the whole. QuantityItem is the item counted/measured; QuantityValue is the amount/measure. Purpose is intended outcome. For like with a category/set, inclusive “such as” is PartPortion;ComparisonRef, while similarity alone is ComparisonRef. SetIteration marks rates and regular correspondences, not event frequency.
